section: FR-80 vs FR-81 — a genuine spec conflict
question: FR-80 names 'an engagement slug' as a navigable entity reference, but FR-81's eight kinds contain no `engagement` and gate test 1 asserts ENTITY_KINDS equals exactly those eight. project-lead ruled engagements render as a plain next/link to the existing /registry/[slug]. Should the spec be amended to record which requirement wins?
best_guess: The ruling is right and should be ratified in writing. Making engagement a ninth kind would fail a gate written before dispatch, and /registry/[slug] already is its detail view. The one cost: an engagement reference that resolves to nothing gets no FR-83 dangling treatment, because a plain link has none — currently unreachable, since slugs come from the row being rendered. A one-line CR-004 stating that FR-80's engagement is served by /registry/[slug] and sits deliberately outside FR-81's closed set would close the conflict.

section: §5a / money — two formatters, now one click apart
question: formatAmount ($111.00) and money (111.00 USD) render the same contract_milestone.amount two ways. Before M2.7 the two screens were not linked; now /committed links each row to /milestones/[id], so one click moves between the two shapes. Which is the product's answer, and may the loser be deleted?
best_guess: Keep formatAmount and delete money. money-display.ts justifies itself on Intl hydration-mismatch grounds, but registry-display.ts pins LOCALE = 'en-US', which defuses that argument. Needs Erik because it edits a file outside this milestone's scope and touches §5a, which is NOT APPROVED.

question: The four-state prose renderer exists in five copies with three incompatible data-verify contracts (prose vs detail-prose, data-verify-state vs data-verify-prose-state) and an `absent` wording split (— vs 'not recorded'). No copy collapses `unreadable` into `absent` — that hazard is refuted. Should a follow-up unit own src/components/ and hoist one implementation?
best_guess: Yes, as its own small work-unit with sole ownership of src/components/. The duplication is a consequence of five parallel Wave C units having no owner for that directory, so it cannot be fixed by any of them without a three-way merge conflict. Not urgent — it does not lie to the operator today — but it fragments every future verification of prose state.

section: FR-81 — EntityDetail identifier has no omit state
question: `identifier?: string | null` conflates 'this entity has no reference' with 'the caller forgot', and omission renders the positive claim 'This <entity> carries no reference of its own.' Four views print their title twice to avoid it. Should the prop become required and discriminated?
best_guess: Yes — make it required as `string | null | "none"`, so omission is a compile error rather than a silent falsehood, and guard identifier="" which currently renders an invisible slot. No view renders the false claim today, so this is a latent trap for the ninth detail view rather than a live defect.

section: Acceptance — the gate that could not run
question: gate:m27:e2e (10 crawl tests over populated screens) is NOT VERIFIED for want of M27_BASE_URL and an aal2 M27_STORAGE_STATE. It fails closed with exit 1 rather than skipping, which is correct. Will Erik run it before M2.7 is marked Complete?
best_guess: It should block the Complete marking. Everything on this branch is exercised against in-memory fakes; run b0952e shipped a dead ingest route behind 966 green tests, and this is the one check positioned to catch the equivalent here. Separately, the failure message names the wrong cause ('Project m27-gate not found'), which will read as a deleted gate rather than an unset variable.
